clue.text: Sentence in visa identifying things you can do?

indicators.note: the sentence is placed in the visa, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a pass is a permit to enter, much like a visa
time is slang for a prison sentence, as in 'doing time'

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders what activities their visa permits, as if a prison term were stamped into the passport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' reads as grammar but is the prisoner's TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbies and recreations are activities a person may choose to do for amusement.

clue.text: Keen insight shown by expert, note, without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the expert and note surround the hesitation

parts.note: an ace is an expert
um is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: An expert shows sharp insight by speaking without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' seems to mean dropping a hesitation; 'without' instead means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdness and sharp judgement amount to keen insight.

clue.text: Puzzles not set (not entirely) producing signs of grief

indicators.note: not here means taking the following letters out of the puzzles

parts.note: teasers are puzzles

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of set is cut off

explanation.surface: Puzzles left unsolved reduce a solver to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying produces drops from the eyes, the visible signs of sorrow.

clue.text: Moneymen unhappy about second source of inspiration

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the second
unhappy means the letters of moneymen are disturbed

explanation.surface: Financiers are unhappy about a second backer for a creative venture.
explanation.walkthrough: Greek goddess of memory and mother of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: As mother of the Muses she is the ultimate origin of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Illuminated initial enveloping line one

indicators.note: enveloping means the start wraps round the other letters

parts.note: the start is the initial stage
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An illuminated initial letter in a manuscript surrounds the first line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit by the stars at night means lit up, illuminated.

clue.text: Go and complain having dropped a glass

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: having dropped tells us the letter a falls out of the complaint word

parts.note: to bleat is to complain feebly

explanation.surface: Someone moans and lets a drinking glass slip from their hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking vessel with a stem and foot is a kind of glass.

clue.text: Stew in large quantities good for Judge

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another, good replacing Judge

parts.note: jumbo means extra large, as in jumbo packs

explanation.surface: A judge says stew in large quantities is good.
explanation.walkthrough: J (Judge) is replaced by G (good) in JUMBO; 'good' and 'Judge' supply those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup-stew from Louisiana, thickened with okra.

clue.text: Online connection: less important way to get together?

parts.note: a B road is a minor road in the UK, below an A road
to band together is to unite

explanation.surface: A minor road is suggested as a route for people to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: UK roads are classed A (major) and B (minor).
explanation.definitionFit: High-speed internet access is the usual connection to the web.

clue.text: Sense certainly retained by rowers?

indicators.note: retained by means the rowers hold the other word inside

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crew of eight rowers
yes is an emphatic certainly

explanation.surface: A rowing crew certainly has sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Not commenting about a tense change

indicators.note: about means the silent word goes around the other letters

parts.note: someone not commenting stays mute
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A spokesman refuses comment on a tense alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter or transform in form is a verb synonym for changing.

clue.text: Openings for members? New role has to accommodate opening for member

indicators.note: to accommodate means the rearranged letters house the single letter inside them
new signals the letters of role has are made into a fresh arrangement
the opening for a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor's new role requires an opening for a member, as in a club or costume.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'members' of the definition are arms, the limbs a garment's sleeve openings admit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeve holes in a garment are gaps through which the limbs (arms) pass.

clue.text: Wet waste deposit turned dry with application of reel

indicators.note: turned means the word for dry is read backwards

parts.note: sec is the wine term for dry
a spool is a reel for thread or film

explanation.surface: Some soggy deposit dried out once a reel was applied to it.
explanation.walkthrough: SEC is French for dry and is used of wines.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit or tank that collects sewage and liquid refuse is a wet waste deposit.

clue.text: Lay down ring road beside important road North

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
the A1 is Britain's main north-south trunk road, written here as AI

explanation.surface: Instructions to lay out a ring road beside a major road heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the long UK trunk road from London to Edinburgh; the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To decree or establish formally is to lay down a rule.

clue.text: The characters in this have something to hide

definitions.text: The characters in this have something to hide

parts.words: The characters in this have something to hide
parts.note: characters are letters, and in coded writing they are arranged to conceal a message

explanation.surface: A novel whose characters all harbour secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people in a story; they are the written symbols of a cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of writing in cipher uses letters and symbols to conceal a secret message.

clue.text: One getting into orbit as moon shot is constrained by economy

indicators.note: is constrained by means the shuffled letters are held inside the economy word

parts.note: a cut is an economy, a saving

indicators.note: shot means the letters of as moon are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A moon shot is held back by budget cuts as a space agency economises.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian space traveller is someone who goes into orbit.

clue.text: Female fight aboard — say — capsized schooners?

indicators.note: aboard puts the female and fight on board the other letters
capsized in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
a lass is a girl
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A woman picks a fight on board a ship, and the schooners overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: Schooners look like sailing ships but are large drinking glasses (sherry or beer).
explanation.definitionFit: Large drinking glasses for sherry or beer are examples of glass vessels.

clue.text: Attractive stone down next to bog

parts.note: to feel down is to feel blue
bog and john are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A pretty stone lies down beside a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The ornamental banded fluorite is mined in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple-banded fluorite prized for ornaments is a decorative stone.

clue.text: Material from The Wall's most unlikely to be covered by a group of executives

indicators.note: to be covered by puts one word inside the other, which covers it

parts.note: a in the sense of 'each', as in 'ten pence a pound', is per
the last person to do something is the most unlikely to do it
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Something from Pink Floyd's The Wall, most improbably sheltered by a company's board.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals in 'The Wall' point to the Pink Floyd album, but any wall will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum sheets lined with paper are the building material used to make interior partitions.

clue.text: British party, mostly a party showing swagger

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rave is a party
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A British political party, mostly a bunch of revellers, shows a lot of swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Boastful showy confidence is a display of swagger.

clue.text: Pointless dropping in with just first two of debutantes — come mob-handed!

indicators.note: dropping means the second in falls out of the phrase

parts.note: something done in vain is pointless

indicators.note: just first two of takes only the opening pair of letters of debutantes

explanation.surface: Pointless debutantes drop in and arrive as a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Mob-handed (British) means in large numbers; an invading force arrives in force.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive in great numbers and overrun a place is to enter as an occupying force.

clue.text: Part of bridal gear I overlooked, taking this group's material

indicators.note: overlooked means the letter I is left out

parts.note: a bride traditionally wears a veil
our means belonging to this group of us

explanation.surface: A wedding outfit lacking one item, and the fabric this team chose for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plush fabric with a pile like velvet is a dress material.

clue.text: Like bad weather in blocking element of sunshine

indicators.note: blocking means in sits inside the ray, blocking it

parts.note: a ray is a beam of sunshine

explanation.surface: Something like bad weather comes in and blocks the sun's rays.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet days with showers are typical of poor weather.

clue.text: Expecting amount to be collected in a vocal performance

indicators.note: to be collected in places the amount inside the other letters

parts.note: to sing is to give a vocal performance
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates a sum being raised at a singing performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposing something will happen is to take it for granted, much like anticipating.

clue.text: Warlike figure chasing 1,000 horses

indicators.note: chasing means the war god comes after the thousand

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A warlike figure chases a thousand horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Female horses are a kind of horse.

clue.text: Painting not quite itemised in possession of arts graduate

indicators.note: in possession of means the graduate holds the other letters inside

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something itemised is on a list

explanation.surface: An arts graduate owns a painting that has not quite been catalogued.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci's portrait of the smiling woman is the world's most famous painting.

clue.text: Heading off for part of golf course for a breather

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the fairway is the mown area between tee and green

explanation.surface: A golfer heads off a section of the course to catch their breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe, a passage carrying air to the lungs, is what a breather needs.

clue.text: Contents of tank (not tyres) providing problems?

indicators.note: contents of means the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: What's in the tank, rather than the tyres, is causing the car trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny, difficult matter is one that presents problems to solve.

clue.text: Go beyond disgruntled voters to get leads in every poll

indicators.note: disgruntled means the letters of voters are put out of order
the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Fed-up voters go too far by taking every poll by storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress a limit is to go past it.
